checks.label: Kernel ASLR (randomize_va_space)
checks.description: ASLR must be set to 2 (full randomization) to prevent memory-based attacks. Value 0=off, 1=partial, 2=full.
checks.remediation: Set full ASLR: echo 2 > /proc/sys/kernel/randomize_va_space. Ensure kernel config has CONFIG_COMPAT_BRK=n.

checks.label: Kernel ASLR Boot Config
checks.description: Kernel boot parameters must not contain norandmaps or nokaslr flags which disable ASLR/KASLR.
checks.remediation: Remove norandmaps and nokaslr from kernel boot cmdline in bootloader config.

checks.label: KASLR (Kernel ASLR)
checks.command: if [ ! -e /proc/config.gz ] && ! ls /boot/config-* >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo 'NOT_OBSERVABLE kernel config not exposed (CONFIG_IKCONFIG_PROC disabled)'; else zcat /proc/config.gz 2>/dev/null | grep 'CONFIG_RANDOMIZE_BASE'; fi
checks.description: Kernel Address Space Layout Randomization randomizes kernel memory layout to prevent kernel exploits. Kernel config options are observable only through /proc/config.gz, which requires CONFIG_IKCONFIG_PROC and is absent on most production Android builds, or through /boot/config-* on a Linux target. When neither is present the check now reports NOT_OBSERVABLE instead of returning an empty result, and NOT_OBSERVABLE is treated as passing because failing a device for absence of evidence would be a false positive.
checks.remediation: Rebuild kernel with CONFIG_RANDOMIZE_BASE=y and ensure nokaslr is not in boot cmdline.

checks.label: PIE - /system/bin/app_process
checks.description: The main Zygote process (app_process) must be compiled as Position Independent Executable (PIE/DYN) for ASLR effectiveness. The grep must apply to whichever readelf call succeeds; without the grouping parentheses the `||` binds before the pipe, so a successful first call bypasses the grep entirely and returns the full unfiltered ELF header instead of the Type: line.
checks.remediation: Rebuild app_process with -fPIE -pie compiler/linker flags. All Android 5.0+ binaries should be PIE.

checks.label: PIE - /system/bin/linker
checks.description: The dynamic linker must be compiled as PIE. A non-PIE linker undermines ASLR for all dynamically linked binaries. The grep must apply to whichever readelf call succeeds; without the grouping parentheses the `||` binds before the pipe, so a successful first call bypasses the grep entirely and returns the full unfiltered ELF header instead of the Type: line.
checks.remediation: Rebuild the system linker with PIE support. This is standard on Android 5.0+.

checks.label: PIE - /system/bin/surfaceflinger
checks.description: SurfaceFlinger is a privileged system service. Must be PIE-compiled to benefit from ASLR.
checks.remediation: Rebuild surfaceflinger with -fPIE -pie flags.

checks.label: PIE - /system/bin/vold
checks.description: Volume daemon (vold) manages storage and runs as root. Must be PIE-compiled.
checks.remediation: Rebuild vold with -fPIE -pie flags.

checks.label: PIE - /system/bin/servicemanager
checks.description: Binder service manager is a critical IPC process. Must be PIE-compiled.
checks.remediation: Rebuild servicemanager with -fPIE -pie flags.

checks.label: Non-PIE Binaries in /system/bin
checks.command: for f in $(ls /system/bin/ 2>/dev/null | head -30); do readelf -h /system/bin/$f 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'EXEC' && echo "NON-PIE: $f"; done 2>/dev/null | head -10
checks.description: Scans critical system binaries for non-PIE (EXEC type) executables which cannot benefit from ASLR.
checks.remediation: Recompile listed non-PIE binaries with -fPIE -pie. All user-space binaries should be PIE on modern Android.

checks.label: Non-PIE Binaries in /vendor/bin
checks.command: for f in $(ls /vendor/bin/ 2>/dev/null | head -30); do readelf -h /vendor/bin/$f 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'EXEC' && echo "NON-PIE: $f"; done 2>/dev/null | head -10
checks.description: Scans vendor binaries for non-PIE executables. Vendor HAL binaries often run with elevated privileges.
checks.remediation: Work with vendor to recompile non-PIE binaries with -fPIE -pie flags.

checks.label: Stack Canary - app_process
checks.description: Stack canaries (__stack_chk_fail) detect buffer overflow attacks. The Zygote process must have stack protection. The grep must apply to whichever readelf call succeeds; without the grouping parentheses the `||` binds before the pipe, so a successful first call bypasses grep -c entirely and returns the full unfiltered symbol table instead of a __stack_chk count, which can pass the old unanchored safe_pattern by accident on any stray digit rather than an actual canary-symbol count.
checks.remediation: Rebuild app_process with -fstack-protector-strong or -fstack-protector-all compiler flags.

checks.label: Stack Canary - linker
checks.description: The dynamic linker must have stack canary protection to prevent exploitation of linker vulnerabilities. The grep must apply to whichever linker binary readelf found (64-bit or 32-bit); without the grouping parentheses the `||` binds before the pipe, so a successful first readelf call returns its entire unfiltered symbol table instead of a __stack_chk count, which both bloats the result and can pass safe_pattern by accident on any digit appearing in the dump rather than on an actual canary-symbol count.
checks.remediation: Rebuild linker with -fstack-protector-strong flag.

checks.label: Stack Canary - surfaceflinger
checks.command: if ! ([ -r /system/bin/surfaceflinger ]); then echo BINARY_NOT_READABLE; else readelf -s /system/bin/surfaceflinger 2>/dev/null | grep -c '__stack_chk'; fi
checks.description: Counts __stack_chk symbols in surfaceflinger. On a production build the adb shell user cannot read /system/bin/surfaceflinger, and 'readelf ... | grep -c' turns that permission denial into the literal string 0, which failed the pattern and scored a finding on every device. The check now reports BINARY_NOT_READABLE and passes, because absence of evidence is not a finding. Verified on a Samsung SM-M025F where app_process is a readable symlink and returns a real count while surfaceflinger is not readable.
checks.remediation: Rebuild surfaceflinger with -fstack-protector-strong flag.

checks.label: RELRO - app_process (Full)
checks.description: Full RELRO makes the GOT read-only after relocation, preventing GOT overwrite attacks on the Zygote. The grep must apply to whichever readelf call succeeds; without the grouping parentheses the `||` binds before the pipe, so a successful first call bypasses grep -c entirely and returns the full unfiltered program-header dump instead of a GNU_RELRO count.
checks.remediation: Rebuild app_process with -Wl,-z,relro,-z,now linker flags for full RELRO protection.

checks.label: RELRO - linker (Full)
checks.description: The dynamic linker must have RELRO to protect its own GOT from overwrite attacks. The grep must apply to whichever readelf call succeeds; without the grouping parentheses the `||` binds before the pipe, so a successful first call bypasses grep -c entirely and returns the full unfiltered program-header dump instead of a GNU_RELRO count.
checks.remediation: Rebuild linker with -Wl,-z,relro,-z,now linker flags.

checks.label: NX (No-Execute) Stack - app_process
checks.description: NX stack prevents code execution from the stack. GNU_STACK must be RW (not RWE) to enforce NX bit. Both greps must apply to whichever readelf call succeeds; without the grouping parentheses the `||` binds before the pipe, so a successful first call bypasses both greps entirely and returns the full unfiltered program-header dump.
checks.remediation: Rebuild app_process with -Wl,-z,noexecstack. Ensure no assembly files use .note.GNU-stack with exec flag.

checks.label: NX Stack - linker
checks.description: Dynamic linker must have NX stack to prevent stack-based code execution. Both greps must apply to whichever readelf call succeeds; without the grouping parentheses the `||` binds before the pipe, so a successful first call bypasses both greps entirely and returns the full unfiltered program-header dump.
checks.remediation: Rebuild linker with -Wl,-z,noexecstack flag.

checks.label: Executable Stack Binaries in /system/bin
checks.command: for f in $(ls /system/bin/ 2>/dev/null | head -30); do readelf -l /system/bin/$f 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'RWE' && echo "EXEC-STACK: $f"; done 2>/dev/null | head -10
checks.description: Binaries with executable stack (RWE) are vulnerable to stack-based code injection attacks.
checks.remediation: Recompile listed binaries with -Wl,-z,noexecstack to remove executable stack permission.

checks.label: FORTIFY_SOURCE - app_process
checks.command: if ! ([ -r /system/bin/app_process64 ] || [ -r /system/bin/app_process ]); then echo BINARY_NOT_READABLE; else (readelf -s /system/bin/app_process64 2>/dev/null || readelf -s /system/bin/app_process 2>/dev/null) | grep -oE '__[A-Za-z0-9_]+_chk' | grep -v '^__stack_chk' | sort -u | wc -l; fi
checks.description: Counts distinct fortified libc wrappers with __stack_chk excluded. Reported as evidence rather than pass or fail: on a Samsung SM-M025F app_process resolves to app_process32, carries two __stack_chk symbols and zero other _chk wrappers, which is normal for a small launcher binary and does not indicate the build omitted FORTIFY_SOURCE.
checks.remediation: Rebuild app_process with -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 compiler flag.

checks.label: FORTIFY_SOURCE - surfaceflinger
checks.command: if ! ([ -r /system/bin/surfaceflinger ]); then echo BINARY_NOT_READABLE; else readelf -s /system/bin/surfaceflinger 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '__[A-Za-z0-9_]+_chk' | grep -v '^__stack_chk' | sort -u | wc -l; fi
checks.description: Counts distinct fortified libc wrappers (__memcpy_chk, __strcpy_chk and similar) with __stack_chk excluded. Reported as evidence rather than pass or fail: a binary that never calls a fortifiable function legitimately imports no wrappers, so a count of zero does not mean the build omitted -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2. Measured on a real device, /system/bin/app_process (a symlink to app_process32) returns zero while carrying stack canaries, which is the case that made the previous high-severity pass/fail wrong. Also reports BINARY_NOT_READABLE where the shell user cannot read the binary.
checks.remediation: Rebuild surfaceflinger with -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 flag.

checks.label: Kernel NX Support
checks.command: cat /proc/cpuinfo 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'nx|xd|xn' | head -1 || dmesg 2>/dev/null | grep -i 'NX.*active' | head -1
checks.description: Hardware NX (No-Execute) bit support is required for effective DEP (Data Execution Prevention).
checks.remediation: Ensure CPU supports NX/XD/XN bit and it is enabled in BIOS/UEFI. ARM64 has XN by default.

checks.label: Kernel Stack Protector
checks.command: if [ ! -e /proc/config.gz ] && ! ls /boot/config-* >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo 'NOT_OBSERVABLE kernel config not exposed (CONFIG_IKCONFIG_PROC disabled)'; else zcat /proc/config.gz 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'STACKPROTECTOR|CC_STACKPROTECTOR' | head -3 || cat /boot/config-* 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'STACKPROTECTOR|CC_STACKPROTECTOR' | head -3; fi
checks.description: Kernel stack protector (CONFIG_STACKPROTECTOR_STRONG) adds canaries to kernel functions to detect stack smashing. Kernel config options are observable only through /proc/config.gz, which requires CONFIG_IKCONFIG_PROC and is absent on most production Android builds, or through /boot/config-* on a Linux target. When neither is present the check now reports NOT_OBSERVABLE instead of returning an empty result, and NOT_OBSERVABLE is treated as passing because failing a device for absence of evidence would be a false positive.
checks.remediation: Rebuild kernel with CONFIG_STACKPROTECTOR=y and CONFIG_STACKPROTECTOR_STRONG=y.

checks.label: Kernel Heap Hardening (SLAB_FREELIST_RANDOM)
checks.command: if [ ! -e /proc/config.gz ] && ! ls /boot/config-* >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo 'NOT_OBSERVABLE kernel config not exposed (CONFIG_IKCONFIG_PROC disabled)'; else zcat /proc/config.gz 2>/dev/null | grep 'SLAB_FREELIST_RANDOM' | head -1 || cat /boot/config-* 2>/dev/null | grep 'SLAB_FREELIST_RANDOM' | head -1; fi
checks.description: Randomized slab freelist makes heap exploitation significantly harder by randomizing allocation order. Kernel config options are observable only through /proc/config.gz, which requires CONFIG_IKCONFIG_PROC and is absent on most production Android builds, or through /boot/config-* on a Linux target. When neither is present the check now reports NOT_OBSERVABLE instead of returning an empty result, and NOT_OBSERVABLE is treated as passing because failing a device for absence of evidence would be a false positive.
checks.remediation: Rebuild kernel with CONFIG_SLAB_FREELIST_RANDOM=y.

checks.label: Kernel Heap Hardening (SLAB_FREELIST_HARDENED)
checks.command: if [ ! -e /proc/config.gz ] && ! ls /boot/config-* >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo 'NOT_OBSERVABLE kernel config not exposed (CONFIG_IKCONFIG_PROC disabled)'; else zcat /proc/config.gz 2>/dev/null | grep 'SLAB_FREELIST_HARDENED' | head -1 || cat /boot/config-* 2>/dev/null | grep 'SLAB_FREELIST_HARDENED' | head -1; fi
checks.description: Hardened freelist adds integrity checks to slab metadata, detecting heap corruption and use-after-free. Kernel config options are observable only through /proc/config.gz, which requires CONFIG_IKCONFIG_PROC and is absent on most production Android builds, or through /boot/config-* on a Linux target. When neither is present the check now reports NOT_OBSERVABLE instead of returning an empty result, and NOT_OBSERVABLE is treated as passing because failing a device for absence of evidence would be a false positive.
checks.remediation: Rebuild kernel with CONFIG_SLAB_FREELIST_HARDENED=y.

checks.label: Kernel CFI (Control Flow Integrity)
checks.command: if [ ! -e /proc/config.gz ] && ! ls /boot/config-* >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo 'NOT_OBSERVABLE kernel config not exposed (CONFIG_IKCONFIG_PROC disabled)'; else zcat /proc/config.gz 2>/dev/null | grep 'CONFIG_CFI_CLANG' | head -1 || cat /boot/config-* 2>/dev/null | grep 'CONFIG_CFI_CLANG' | head -1; fi
checks.description: Clang CFI prevents control-flow hijacking by validating indirect function calls at runtime. Kernel config options are observable only through /proc/config.gz, which requires CONFIG_IKCONFIG_PROC and is absent on most production Android builds, or through /boot/config-* on a Linux target. When neither is present the check now reports NOT_OBSERVABLE instead of returning an empty result, and NOT_OBSERVABLE is treated as passing because failing a device for absence of evidence would be a false positive.
checks.remediation: Rebuild kernel with CONFIG_CFI_CLANG=y using Clang compiler with LTO enabled.

checks.label: Kernel Shadow Call Stack
checks.command: if [ ! -e /proc/config.gz ] && ! ls /boot/config-* >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo 'NOT_OBSERVABLE kernel config not exposed (CONFIG_IKCONFIG_PROC disabled)'; else zcat /proc/config.gz 2>/dev/null | grep 'SHADOW_CALL_STACK' | head -1 || cat /boot/config-* 2>/dev/null | grep 'SHADOW_CALL_STACK' | head -1; fi
checks.description: Shadow Call Stack protects return addresses in a separate stack, preventing ROP attacks on ARM64. Kernel config options are observable only through /proc/config.gz, which requires CONFIG_IKCONFIG_PROC and is absent on most production Android builds, or through /boot/config-* on a Linux target. When neither is present the check now reports NOT_OBSERVABLE instead of returning an empty result, and NOT_OBSERVABLE is treated as passing because failing a device for absence of evidence would be a false positive.
checks.remediation: Rebuild kernel with CONFIG_SHADOW_CALL_STACK=y (ARM64 only, requires Clang compiler).

checks.label: Kernel KASAN (Address Sanitizer)
checks.command: if [ ! -e /proc/config.gz ] && ! ls /boot/config-* >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo 'NOT_OBSERVABLE kernel config not exposed (CONFIG_IKCONFIG_PROC disabled)'; else zcat /proc/config.gz 2>/dev/null | grep 'CONFIG_KASAN' | head -1 || dmesg 2>/dev/null | grep -i kasan | head -1; fi
checks.description: Kernel Address Sanitizer detects out-of-bounds and use-after-free bugs. Usually enabled in debug/test builds. Kernel config options are observable only through /proc/config.gz, which requires CONFIG_IKCONFIG_PROC and is absent on most production Android builds, or through /boot/config-* on a Linux target. When neither is present the check now reports NOT_OBSERVABLE instead of returning an empty result, and NOT_OBSERVABLE is treated as passing because failing a device for absence of evidence would be a false positive.
checks.remediation: Enable CONFIG_KASAN=y for testing builds. Note: significant performance overhead, not for production.

checks.label: Kernel HARDENED_USERCOPY
checks.command: if [ ! -e /proc/config.gz ] && ! ls /boot/config-* >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo 'NOT_OBSERVABLE kernel config not exposed (CONFIG_IKCONFIG_PROC disabled)'; else zcat /proc/config.gz 2>/dev/null | grep 'HARDENED_USERCOPY' | head -1 || cat /boot/config-* 2>/dev/null | grep 'HARDENED_USERCOPY' | head -1; fi
checks.description: Hardened usercopy validates that copy_from_user/copy_to_user operations stay within expected slab bounds. Kernel config options are observable only through /proc/config.gz, which requires CONFIG_IKCONFIG_PROC and is absent on most production Android builds, or through /boot/config-* on a Linux target. When neither is present the check now reports NOT_OBSERVABLE instead of returning an empty result, and NOT_OBSERVABLE is treated as passing because failing a device for absence of evidence would be a false positive.
checks.remediation: Rebuild kernel with CONFIG_HARDENED_USERCOPY=y.

checks.label: Kernel INIT_ON_ALLOC/FREE
checks.command: if [ ! -e /proc/config.gz ] && ! ls /boot/config-* >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo 'NOT_OBSERVABLE kernel config not exposed (CONFIG_IKCONFIG_PROC disabled)'; else zcat /proc/config.gz 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'INIT_ON_ALLOC_DEFAULT_ON|INIT_ON_FREE_DEFAULT_ON' | head -2 || cat /boot/config-* 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'INIT_ON_ALLOC_DEFAULT_ON|INIT_ON_FREE_DEFAULT_ON' | head -2; fi
checks.description: Zero-initializing heap memory on allocation/free prevents info leaks from uninitialized memory and use-after-free. Kernel config options are observable only through /proc/config.gz, which requires CONFIG_IKCONFIG_PROC and is absent on most production Android builds, or through /boot/config-* on a Linux target. When neither is present the check now reports NOT_OBSERVABLE instead of returning an empty result, and NOT_OBSERVABLE is treated as passing because failing a device for absence of evidence would be a false positive.
checks.remediation: Rebuild kernel with CONFIG_INIT_ON_ALLOC_DEFAULT_ON=y and CONFIG_INIT_ON_FREE_DEFAULT_ON=y.

checks.label: mmap_min_addr Protection
checks.description: mmap_min_addr prevents mapping memory at low addresses (NULL page), blocking NULL pointer dereference exploits.
checks.remediation: Set minimum mmap address: echo 65536 > /proc/sys/vm/mmap_min_addr

checks.label: Kernel dmesg Restriction
checks.description: Restricting dmesg to root prevents unprivileged users from reading kernel log which may leak KASLR offsets.
checks.remediation: Restrict kernel log access: echo 1 > /proc/sys/kernel/dmesg_restrict

checks.label: Kernel kptr_restrict
checks.description: kptr_restrict hides kernel pointer addresses from /proc/kallsyms, preventing KASLR bypass via info leak.
checks.remediation: Restrict kernel pointers: echo 2 > /proc/sys/kernel/kptr_restrict

checks.label: Kernel perf_event Restriction
checks.description: perf_event_paranoid >= 2 prevents unprivileged access to performance counters used in side-channel attacks.
checks.remediation: Restrict perf events: echo 3 > /proc/sys/kernel/perf_event_paranoid

checks.label: Kernel Modules Disabled
checks.description: Disabling kernel module loading after boot prevents rootkits from loading malicious kernel modules.
checks.remediation: Lock module loading post-boot: echo 1 > /proc/sys/kernel/modules_disabled (irreversible until reboot).

checks.label: Shared Library RELRO Check (/system/lib64)
checks.command: for f in $(ls /system/lib64/*.so 2>/dev/null | head -10); do readelf -l $f 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'GNU_RELRO' || echo "NO-RELRO: $(basename $f)"; done 2>/dev/null | head -5
checks.description: System shared libraries without RELRO are vulnerable to GOT overwrite attacks.
checks.remediation: Recompile libraries without RELRO using -Wl,-z,relro,-z,now linker flags.

checks.label: readelf Availability
checks.description: readelf is required for binary hardening analysis. If absent, PIE/RELRO/NX/canary checks will return empty.
checks.remediation: Push readelf to device: adb push readelf /data/local/tmp/ && chmod +x /data/local/tmp/readelf
